contract_plain_english: For the basic unshifted softmax algorithm, each numerator exponential has relative error at most u, the recursively summed denominator has first-order relative error at most (n+1)u, and the final division contributes another error at most u. Their composition gives relative error at most (n+3)u + O(u^2) in every component, then the same coefficient in the relative infinity-norm bound of Theorem 3.3. The result excludes overflow and underflow and inherits the assumed accuracy of exp. [PDF p. 6, anchor: Algorithm 3.1 and standing assumption; PDF p. 8, anchor: componentwise derivation following equation (3.5); PDF p. 9, anchor: Theorem 3.3, equation (3.6)]

source_evidence.observation: Basic arithmetic uses the standard relative-error model with unit roundoff u. [PDF p. 4, anchor: equation (1.7)]

The basic algorithm computes unshifted exponentials, their recursive sum, and then each softmax component by dividing the corresponding exponential by that sum; overflow and underflow are excluded. [PDF p. 6, anchor: Algorithm 3.1 and standing assumption]

source_evidence.anchor: componentwise basic-softmax error derivation following equation (3.5)
source_evidence.observation: The exponential, denominator, and division errors are composed to obtain hat(g_j) = g_j(1 + tau_j), with |tau_j| <= (n+3)u + O(u^2) for every component. [PDF p. 8, anchor: componentwise derivation following equation (3.5)]
Theorem 3.3 weakens the componentwise result to the infinity-norm relative forward-error bound ||g-hat(g)||_infinity/||g||_infinity <= (n+3)u + O(u^2). [PDF p. 9, anchor: Theorem 3.3, equation (3.6)]

statement.algorithm_linkage: The result applies specifically to Algorithm 3.1: compute w_i = exp(x_i), recursively accumulate s, and return g_i = w_i/s by floating-point division. It does not apply to formula (1.5) or Algorithm 4.1. [PDF p. 6, anchor: Algorithm 3.1; PDF p. 9, anchor: Theorem 3.3 and transition to equation (3.7)]
binders: The input is x in R^n, and softmax components are indexed j = 1,...,n. [PDF p. 6, anchor: Algorithm 3.1]
The exact denominator is s := sum_{i=1}^n exp(x_i), and the exact component is g_j := exp(x_j)/s. [PDF p. 1, anchor: equation (1.2); PDF p. 6, anchor: Algorithm 3.1]

hat(s) is the recursively computed denominator and hat(g_j) is the component returned by the final division in Algorithm 3.1. [PDF p. 6, anchor: Algorithm 3.1; PDF p. 8, anchor: componentwise derivation following equation (3.5)]

delta_1 denotes exponential-evaluation error, delta_2 denotes division error, eta denotes relative denominator error, and tau_j denotes the resulting componentwise relative error. [PDF p. 8, anchor: componentwise derivation following equation (3.5)]
conclusions: For each j, hat(g_j) = exp(x_j)(1+delta_1)(1+delta_2)/hat(s). [PDF p. 8, anchor: first display in the componentwise softmax derivation]
Substituting hat(s) = s(1+eta) gives hat(g_j) = exp(x_j)(1+delta_1)(1+delta_2)/(s(1+eta)), with |eta| <= (n+1)u + O(u^2). [PDF p. 8, anchor: second display in the componentwise softmax derivation]
For every component j, hat(g_j) = g_j(1+tau_j), where |tau_j| <= (n+3)u + O(u^2). [PDF p. 8, anchor: final componentwise display following equation (3.5)]
Consequently, ||g-hat(g)||_infinity/||g||_infinity <= (n+3)u + O(u^2). [PDF p. 9, anchor: Theorem 3.3, equation (3.6)]
The paper characterizes the componentwise result as guaranteeing relative error of order at most nu in every component. [PDF p. 8, anchor: sentence immediately before Theorem 3.3]
The deterministic bound becomes uninformative when n is of order 1/u or larger; the paper notes that this can occur at n = 2048 in fp16. [PDF p. 9, anchor: discussion following equation (3.6)]
constants_and_indexing: The component index j ranges from 1 through n. [PDF p. 1, anchor: equation (1.2); PDF p. 8, anchor: componentwise derivation]

The first-order constant n+3 consists of the inherited n+1 denominator bound plus one exponential-error contribution and one division-error contribution. [PDF p. 8, anchor: componentwise error composition]
The bound has no explicit dependence on the magnitudes or range of the x_i. [PDF p. 8, anchor: componentwise bound; PDF p. 9, anchor: equation (3.6)]
definitions_and_conventions: The exact softmax g is the gradient of log-sum-exp and has components exp(x_j)/sum_i exp(x_i). [PDF p. 1, anchor: equation (1.2)]
Theorem 3.3 is obtained by weakening the preceding componentwise relative-error bound to a normwise bound. [PDF p. 8, anchor: sentence before Theorem 3.3; PDF p. 9, anchor: equation (3.6)]
The logarithm computed by Algorithm 3.1 does not enter this softmax error composition; the softmax divisions reuse the accumulated sum s. [PDF p. 6, anchor: Algorithm 3.1, lines 6-9]
error_notions: The derivation first gives componentwise relative forward error, hat(g_j) = g_j(1+tau_j). [PDF p. 8, anchor: final componentwise display following equation (3.5)]
The theorem gives normwise relative forward error for the whole vector. [PDF p. 9, anchor: equation (3.6)]
The result is not a backward-error statement and does not bound violation of the normalization sum directly. [PDF p. 8, anchor: componentwise derivation; PDF p. 9, anchor: Theorem 3.3]
exceptional_values: Overflow and underflow are expressly excluded. [PDF p. 9, anchor: Theorem 3.3 hypothesis]
The theorem does not specify behavior for NaNs, infinities, zero denominators caused by exceptional arithmetic, or non-real inputs. [PDF p. 6, anchor: Algorithm 3.1; PDF p. 9, anchor: Theorem 3.3]
higher_order_terms: Both componentwise and normwise bounds retain O(u^2). [PDF p. 8, anchor: final componentwise display; PDF p. 9, anchor: equation (3.6)]
No explicit coefficient or uniform range is supplied for the O(u^2) remainder. [PDF p. 7, anchor: paragraph explaining O(u^2); PDF p. 9, anchor: equation (3.6)]
hypotheses: The algorithm is the basic unshifted Algorithm 3.1, not the shifted algorithm or the division-free alternative. [PDF p. 6, anchor: Algorithm 3.1; PDF p. 9, anchor: Theorem 3.3 title]
No overflow or underflow occurs. [PDF p. 6, anchor: Section 3 standing assumption; PDF p. 9, anchor: Theorem 3.3 hypothesis]
The computed exponential satisfies a relative-error bound |delta_1| <= u. [PDF p. 7, anchor: equation (3.1); PDF p. 8, anchor: softmax derivation following equation (3.5)]
The final division contributes a relative error delta_2 with |delta_2| <= u. [PDF p. 8, anchor: first display in the softmax derivation]
The recursively computed denominator can be written hat(s) = s(1 + eta), with |eta| <= (n+1)u + O(u^2). [PDF p. 8, anchor: equation (3.3) as used in the softmax derivation]
implicit_context: The denominator estimate and its n+1 coefficient are inherited from the positive recursive-summation analysis culminating in equation (3.3). [PDF p. 8, anchor: equation (3.3) and its use in the softmax derivation]

The paper calls the n term pessimistic and cites probabilistic rounding-error models under which it can be replaced by a small constant multiple of sqrt(n) with high probability; that statement is not part of deterministic Theorem 3.3. [PDF p. 9, anchor: discussion following equation (3.6)]
norms: Theorem 3.3 uses the vector infinity norm in both numerator and denominator. [PDF p. 9, anchor: equation (3.6)]
The denominator of the normwise relative error is the exact ||g||_infinity. [PDF p. 9, anchor: equation (3.6)]
numerical_model: Basic arithmetic operations obey fl(a op b) = (a op b)(1+delta), |delta| <= u. [PDF p. 4, anchor: equation (1.7)]
The exponential is treated as having relative error at most u, separately from the basic-operation model. [PDF p. 7, anchor: equation (3.1)]
The denominator is formed by ordinary recursive summation, whose accumulated first-order relative error is bounded by (n+1)u. [PDF p. 6, anchor: Algorithm 3.1; PDF p. 8, anchor: equation (3.3)]
The result is precision-generic through u; fp16 appears only in the subsequent illustration of when the bound loses usefulness. [PDF p. 9, anchor: discussion following equation (3.6)]

undebatable_constraints: The contract is for the basic unshifted softmax implementation in Algorithm 3.1. [PDF p. 6, anchor: Algorithm 3.1; PDF p. 9, anchor: Theorem 3.3 title]
The componentwise conclusion applies separately to every j and has first-order constant n+3. [PDF p. 8, anchor: final componentwise display following equation (3.5)]
The theorem's vector conclusion is a relative infinity-norm forward-error bound. [PDF p. 9, anchor: equation (3.6)]
The absence of overflow and underflow is mandatory. [PDF p. 9, anchor: Theorem 3.3 hypothesis]
The O(u^2) term must not be dropped or represented as an explicit zero remainder. [PDF p. 9, anchor: equation (3.6)]
